title: unified-rollouts: transparent metric-matching and multi-metric auto-rollback enhancements
author: Daniel Brooks
description:
Motivation: Improve safety and transparency of unified rollouts by introducing a metric-matching layer and extending the auto-rollback controller to support multi-metric thresholds and per-traffic-segment rollback actions. This PR implements a transparent metric-matching stage that aligns incoming rollout metrics with the rollout config schema (canary/A-B/shadow) and normalizes histograms/latency buckets for consistent comparisons across model variants. It also extends the autorollback controller to: (1) evaluate multiple metrics with configurable aggregators and severity weights, (2) support per-segment thresholds (e.g. high-latency tail on mobile region, error-rate on critical routes), and (3) execute configurable rollback actions (scale-down, divert-to-fallback, pause-rollout, promote-to-shadow).

What changed (high level): added a metric-matching pipeline in the rollout controller, multi-metric evaluation logic with weighted scoring, new rollout config fields + validation, integration tests and e2e canary simulation harness, docs and CLI examples, and minor serving runtime hooks to emit tagged metrics for segment-aware evaluation.

API / Config changes: new rollout spec fields under "strategy.metrics": (1) metrics: list of {name, source, aggregator, weight, threshold{op,val}, segment_selector}, (2) rollback_actions: ordered list of {action, scope, delay, params}. The controller validates backward compatibility: existing single-metric configs continue to work.

Migration notes: no immediate migration required. Existing rollouts will continue using legacy behavior unless the new metrics section is present. Operators can opt-in to the new behavior by updating rollout YAMLs and adding metric mappings. A CLI migration helper (rolloutctl migrate-metrics) is included.

Testing & safety: added unit tests for metric normalization and scoring, integration tests that simulate canary traffic with synthetic latency/error distributions, and an e2e scenario that exercises rollback_actions including pause and divert-to-fallback. CI previously flaked on one integration test (canary simulation timing); fixed by introducing deterministic time mocking and increased test timeout.

Performance: metric-matching pipeline adds negligible overhead (~0.7ms median per-evaluation on benchmark harness) compared to previous controller loop; batching retained for evaluation windows.

Docs: updated rollout strategy docs with examples for A/B, canary and shadow scenarios, and a migration guide.

Related: ENG-2413 tracks follow-up for adaptive weighting heuristics, ENG-2499 for rollout observability dashboards.
